newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB says railcar unloads at ports below target.
newsitem.headline: CWB says railcar unloads at ports below target.

text.p: Railcar unloads at export ports in the week ended Sunday were well below target levels, the Canadian Wheat Board said.
Weather and equipment failure have delayed shipments of grains and oilseeds to Pacific ports since early January and a blizzard in Manitoba this weekend caused more rail delays.

Manitoba's blizzard set provincial records for the most snow accumulated in a 24 hour period in April at 35.0 cm, and as the longest blizzard on record with visibility reduced to less than one km for 24 hours and 10 minutes.
A total of 48.2 cm (20 inches) fell on Winnipeg over the weekend, Environment Canada said.
Vancouver saw 1,873 railcars unloaded compared to the target of 3,300 hopper cars. The prior week saw 2,523 unloads.
Prince Rupert unloads totalled 1,172 hopper cars compared to the target of 1,300 railcars. The prior week saw 1,404 unloads.
Thunder Bay saw 1,280 railcar unloads compared to the target of 1,400 hopper cars. The prior week saw 836 unloads.
